title: The Ewe found Notsié
description: Ewe migrants pressed westward by the Yoruba settle the last stop of their journey and ring Notsié with a great wall, the town from which their exodus becomes legend.

title: Togoland becomes German
description: Gustav Nachtigal signs a treaty with Chief Mlapa III at Togoville, and the coast between the British and French becomes Germany's model colony.

title: Capital moves to Lomé
description: The German seat of government shifts from malarial Aného to the planned grid of Lomé with its pier and railways.

title: Allies take Togoland
description: Three weeks into the First World War the Germans blow up the Kamina wireless station and surrender, the first Allied victory of the war.

title: League mandates split Togoland
description: The League of Nations divides the colony: Britain takes the western third toward the Gold Coast and France the east, the core of today's Togo.

title: Lomé tax riots
description: A tax increase as incomes fall provokes days of riots in Lomé, a major political break under the mandate.

title: UN trust territory
description: French Togoland becomes a United Nations trust territory, committed to progress toward self-government.

title: Autonomous republic
description: A French referendum makes Togo an autonomous republic; the same year the British zone votes to leave the colony and join the Gold Coast.

title: Independence from France
description: Togo becomes independent with Sylvanus Olympio as its first president.

title: Olympio assassinated
description: Ex-soldiers denied places in a shrunken army shoot the president at the American embassy gate, Africa's first coup d'état after independence.

title: Eyadéma seizes power
description: Army chief Étienne Eyadéma overthrows President Grunitzky and rules, at first without office, then in uniform as colonel-president.

title: One-party state
description: Eyadéma founds the Rally of the Togolese People and outlaws every other party.

title: Mercenary attack on Lomé
description: Commandos in lorries try to decapitate the regime at night; French jets and Zairian paratroops fly in to save Eyadéma.

title: Sovereign National Conference
description: After months of strikes, a national conference strips Eyadéma of most powers and names a transitional prime minister; soldiers besiege him that autumn.

title: Multiparty constitution
description: A referendum approves a democratic constitution, but the army keeps breaking the transition back to Eyadéma's side.

title: Eyadéma dies; his son is installed
description: The president dies after 38 years in power and the army puts up his son Faure Gnassingbé, until African pressure forces an election.

title: Faure Gnassingbé elected amid violence
description: Faure wins the rushed vote and security forces kill several hundred as protesters and refugees flee to Benin and Ghana.

title: Faure wins again
description: With the opposition split, the president wins a third term on the first round.

title: Mass protests for term limits
description: Hundreds of thousands march for a two-term limit and the end of a half century of family rule; talks fail and the movement is banned from the streets.
